claims.text: The Bharatiya Janata Party emerged as the single largest party in Rajasthan's urban local body elections, winning 4,179 wards out of 10,235 declared wards.
In the Rajasthan urban local body polls, Congress won 3,613 wards and independent candidates won 2,273 wards.
The BJP secured clear majorities in four municipal corporations in Rajasthan: Jaipur, Bhilwara, Kota, and Udaipur.
In Jhalawar, Congress won the municipal council, taking control of a former stronghold of former chief minister Vasundhara Raje.
The Aam Aadmi Party made its political debut in Rajasthan by winning control of its maiden municipal body in Baran.
In Chief Minister Bhajan Lal Sharma's home turf of Bharatpur, independents won 36 wards, BJP won 20 wards, and Congress won seven wards.
The State Election Commission postponed chairperson and deputy chairperson elections in Jaipur, Jodhpur, Kota municipal corporations, and Suket municipality due to EVM technical glitches.
The State Election Commission ordered repolling at 10 polling stations in Jaipur, Jodhpur, Kota, and Suket for September 16, with counting scheduled for September 17.
The BJP secured 55 out of 100 wards in the Kota Municipal Corporation election to cross the majority threshold.
Congress candidate Laxmi Sharma sat on a dharna outside JDB College in Kota demanding transparency after counting in Ward 87 was put on hold due to EVM malfunction.
In Bundi, three independent candidates—Prabhat Devi, Aatmaram Chopdar, and Vishal Sharma—joined the BJP after the election, giving the party a full majority.
Congress won 42 of 80 wards in Bikaner Municipal Corporation to secure a majority.
In Jodhpur Municipal Corporation, BJP and Congress tied with 44 wards each in the 100-member body.
In Ajmer, Congress emerged as the largest party winning 37 of 80 wards, while BJP won 32 and Independents won 11.
More than 1.44 crore voters were eligible to vote across 309 urban local bodies in Rajasthan in two phases on September 9 and 11.
Rajasthan Congress president Govind Singh Dotasra stated that the BJP's lead over Congress in this election was less than one percentage point.
21-year-old Congress candidate Faiz Hasan won Ward 71 in Jaipur Municipal Corporation with 5,426 votes.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi hailed the BJP's victory in Rajasthan civic polls on X, describing it as proof of the 'victory of truth over the echo of falsehood'.
Union Home Minister Amit Shah stated in Mumbai that he is confident the Uniform Civil Code will be introduced in 21 BJP-NDA ruled states before 2029.
TDP parliamentary party leader Lavu Sri Krishna Devarayalu stated that TDP will involve various stakeholders before adopting the Uniform Civil Code in Andhra Pradesh.
JD(U) working president Sanjay Jha stated that he will meet Union Home Minister Amit Shah to discuss the Uniform Civil Code issue.
LJP (Ram Vilas) chief Chirag Paswan called for the Uniform Civil Code proposal to be made public and undergo comprehensive consultation before his party states its position.
JD(U) MLA Shyam Rajak stated that the Uniform Civil Code will never be implemented in Bihar at any cost.
HAM (S) national president Santosh Kumar Suman stated that if Home Minister Amit Shah proposed UCC, there must be good things in it, and alliance leaders would be taken into confidence.
RJD spokesperson Shakti Yadav stated that the RJD will never allow the Uniform Civil Code to be implemented in Bihar.
AIMIM president Asaduddin Owaisi stated that a Uniform Civil Code is not about equality but about targeting Muslims and imposing Hindu law on non-Hindus.
Uttarakhand passed the Uniform Civil Code Act in February 2024 and fully enforced it on January 27, 2025.
The Gujarat Legislative Assembly passed the Gujarat Uniform Civil Code in March 2026.
The Assam Legislative Assembly passed the Uniform Civil Code, Assam, Bill in May 2026, while exempting members of Scheduled Tribes.
The Madhya Pradesh Legislative Assembly passed the Madhya Pradesh Uniform Civil Code Bill in July 2026.
Maharashtra, West Bengal, and Chhattisgarh have formed committees to draft Uniform Civil Code legislation.
The Central Bureau of Investigation registered an FIR on September 13 to probe the death of celebrity manager Disha Salian under IPC sections for gang rape, murder, and destruction of evidence.
Disha Salian died on June 8, 2020, after falling from the 14th floor of a residential building in Mumbai.

The CBI FIR mentions several individuals whose roles require investigation, including Aaditya Thackeray, Dino Morea, Rhea Chakraborty, Uddhav Thackeray, and Sachin Vaze, though no one is formally named as an accused.
A division bench of the Bombay High Court directed the CBI on September 2 to register an FIR into Disha Salian's death based on a statement by her father, Satish Salian.
The Bombay High Court stated that the failure of Mumbai Police to register an FIR for six years raised questions and noted glaring discrepancies in the prior investigation.
Actor Sushant Singh Rajput was found dead at his residence on June 14, 2020, six days after Disha Salian's death.
Satish Salian recorded a fresh statement at the CBI's Bandra-Kurla Complex office in Mumbai on September 12.
The CBI FIR alleges extraordinary contradictions and suppression of records regarding the seizure and use of Disha Salian's mobile phone.
NCP (SP) leader Supriya Sule expressed surprise at the CBI registering an FIR, noting that the same government had previously closed the case.
AIMIM leader Waris Pathan stated that the Disha Salian case should not be given political color and should be left for the court to decide.
Satish Salian's lawyer Nilesh Ojha stated that the CBI FIR invokes IPC Sections 376D, 302, 201, 217, 218, and 120B.
